transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello. Well... I suppose it's my driving. 

Whenever my car reaches one of those long bridges... the ones heading toward Miami... I just... my chest tightens up. I end up clamping my hands on the steering wheel, and I get this sudden, overwhelming feeling that I absolutely have to get off the bridge right then. Even though there's nowhere to go. 

So... that's why I'm here.
Do you ever experience similar feelings of chest tightness or panic in other situations, like in crowds, while using public transportation, or when you're in a confined space?
No... I don't think so. I haven't noticed anything like that in those sorts of places. It's... just the bridges.
Have you ever experienced these panic-like feelings in other specific situations, such as driving through tunnels, on highways, or at high altitudes?
No... highways are fine. I don't really go anywhere with high altitudes, but... no. Like I said, it's just the bridges.
Have you ever felt this kind of panic or intense fear in any other specific situations, even if they’re not related to driving or bridges—like flying, seeing a spider, or being in a social setting?
No... nothing like that. Spiders are just bugs, and... well, I do fine around people. I really haven't had this happen with anything else. Just... what I mentioned.
Do you find yourself avoiding driving over those bridges altogether, or do you only feel the panic when you’re actually on them?

I... I try not to go over them at all anymore. I've been saying no to things. Gallery openings... my birdwatching trips. Even... well, even seeing my daughter sometimes, unless someone else can drive me. It's... hard to admit. I've always been the one who took care of things, who drove everywhere. It's embarrassing.
Have you ever felt this same kind of panic on other types of bridges, like shorter ones, or ones that aren’t heading toward Miami?
No... I haven't. Just the ones I mentioned. Shorter bridges are fine, I don't... I don't feel anything on those. It's just the big ones.
